A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching. v2 adds clarifications, algorithm boxes, and a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original stochastic-system simulations, prediction errors in Table 1, runtime measurements in Appendix B.4, and density-prediction and exploration results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation outcomes, prediction-error table, runtime measurements, and supplementary results in Appendices B.4 and C.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the documented density-based Monte Carlo probability computation: v1 averages density-weighted indicators, whereas v2 explicitly samples from the estimated density and averages unweighted indicators. The core density estimator, kernel regressors, and safe-sampling rule remain unchanged; the new algorithm boxes mostly document existing modules.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic two-dimensional navigation system, safety/reset regions, and test-control scenarios. Appendix C retains the same density-prediction cases and information-gain experiments. Higher-dimensional and physical-system evaluations remain future work.

E2.justification: Both compare the same safety/reset threshold variants, including the unconstrained setting. Neither reports an evaluated external safe-learning baseline. v2 adds a related-work citation and mentions future safe-RL comparisons, without adding comparators to the experiments.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the two-parameter controls, 1000 iterations, 500 simulation steps, threshold settings, 200-path sampling, and 100-sample Monte Carlo reference estimates for 1000 predictions. Appendix C retains the same evaluation grid and controls. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The threshold-dependent exploration analysis, three-control density-prediction case study in Figure 7, and information-gain analysis in Figure 8 are retained. Added discussion and reformatted plots introduce no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports the same MSE and standard-deviation statistics in both versions. Runtime measurements remain based on 20 repeated runs in Appendix B.4. The new checklist restates existing uncertainty reporting rather than introducing additional runs or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 values are identical, including safety MSE 0.7010 ± 0.3847 at ε = ξ = 0.1. The reported 31.77 ± 0.38 minute training runtime and the plotted outcomes and qualitative findings in Figures 1–8 are also retained.

T1.justification: Assumption (A3) strengthens ν > n/2 to ν > max(n, m+1)/2. Lemma A.6 replaces the critical Sobolev embedding with H^(n/2+ε), revises the derivation and rate accordingly, and adds exponent qualifications. Appendix A also corrects n/N normalization and indexing and the final inequality direction in Lemma A.5. These are targeted mathematical corrections within the existing theorem framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and central safe-learning and adaptive-rate contributions are retained. The conclusion newly asserts polynomial dimensional dependence and mitigation of the curse of dimensionality under sufficient smoothness, while explicitly qualifying the empirical validation as low-dimensional.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the connection between coefficient regularity and density regularity as expected but requiring future formal analysis, where v1 presented it as established under suitable conditions. Remark 1 expands the dependence on prior RKHS-norm bounds and its exploration cost. The conclusion adds limitations concerning dimensional validation, baseline comparisons, and kernel/threshold selection.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds module-level pseudocode, explicitly documenting density sampling, storage of the regularized matrix inverse, and precomputation of safety/reset coefficients. Hardware, runtime, and tuning information are retained. The repository reference added to the introduction was already supplied in v1's Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al.'s work on safe time-varying optimization to Section 2.1 and Shalev-Shwartz's online-learning reference for the proposed future use of the doubling trick. The broader related-work discussion and claimed distinction of joint safe exploration and density estimation remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations of initial sets, trajectory notation, confidence parameters, and the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. It also updates the publication header and an email address. The main narrative and Section 1–7/Appendix A–C organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 receive more regular panel arrangements, and Figures 2–4 and 6 gain explicit threshold labels and revised captions. Table 1's caption moves above the table. Appendix B adds three algorithm boxes; the existing sampling algorithm is renumbered from 1 to 4. These display changes retain the experimental content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the stronger smoothness condition and revised Sobolev-embedding argument, and improves usability through explicit pseudocode and clearer figure labels. Its expanded limitations better delimit the existing evidence. The stronger assumptions and slightly qualified rates narrow the guarantees appropriately; these targeted gains improve the paper without establishing a broader empirical contribution.
